name: Susan Electricals India Ltd
tagline: Just-listed small-cap maker of aluminium/copper winding wires, conductors and power cables for DISCOMs -- riding the grid-capex wave with 250%+ YoY revenue growth and a 60% capacity expansion, but the product is a commodity and the returns ratios flatter a tiny post-IPO equity base
business_overview: Susan Electricals India (BSE: 544793, recently listed) manufactures aluminium- and copper-based electrical winding wires, conductors and power cables. It sells primarily to state electricity distribution companies (DISCOMs), EPC contractors, infrastructure companies and electrical-product OEMs. Revenue grew from ~Rs 49 Cr (FY21) to ~Rs 269 Cr (FY26); Q1 FY27 revenue ~Rs 95 Cr, +254% YoY. Capacity is being expanded ~60%.
fundamentals_table: ~37% / ~64.6% (3-yr ROE ~54% -- inflated by a small post-IPO equity base)
~Rs 269 Cr FY26 (~449% over 5 years); Q1 FY27 ~Rs 95 Cr, +254% YoY
~196% PAT CAGR over 5 years (off a tiny base)
fundamentals_narrative: The growth is real and the balance sheet is currently clean, but two cautions: (1) winding wire / ACSR-type conductors are a fragmented commodity where realisations track LME aluminium/copper plus a thin conversion spread -- there is no pricing power; (2) ROE in the 50-64% band is a function of a very small equity base just after a SME-scale IPO and will normalise sharply as the balance sheet grows to fund the capex and working capital. DISCOM receivables are a structural working-capital risk in this customer segment.
technical_read: Not pulled. Trading in the upper half of a wide post-listing range.

Third-party coverage frames it as a grid-modernisation beneficiary and debates whether 279% revenue growth justifies the post-listing rally.

bse_notes: No corporate-action red flags identified in the available window. Standard small/recently-listed-company caveats apply (limited public history, thin float).
bull_case: Direct exposure to a priority-1, accelerating theme -- grid / transmission equipment (conductors, cables) as India ramps distribution capex
Explosive recent growth (Q1 FY27 revenue +254% YoY) with a ~60% capacity expansion underway
High headline ROCE/ROE and currently low leverage
Undemanding-looking ~26x P/E relative to the growth rate
bear_case: Winding wire / conductors are a commodity -- realisation is metal price plus a thin conversion margin, no moat
ROE 50-64% is a small-post-IPO-equity-base artefact and will compress materially as the company scales
DISCOM / EPC customer base carries structural receivables and payment-cycle risk
Very short listed history; growth is off a tiny base and may not annualise
Capex + working capital will require external funding, diluting the clean balance sheet
verdict_headline: A genuine grid-capex growth story at an early, high-risk stage -- label allowed only on the small-cap live-inflection carve-out; conviction Low-Medium, unconfirmed
verdict_reasoning: Conviction: Low-Medium - assigned via Confluence methodology

disclaimer: This is independent research for informational purposes only, not investment advice.

four_box.note: Grid/DISCOM T&D capex is a genuine structural multi-year theme (tailwind=yes). Q1FY27 confirms live small-cap inflection: rev +254% YoY (Rs95.4cr), PAT turned positive from a loss, margin 4.18%->11.9%, capacity expanding 60% (7,500->12,000km/yr, commercial Feb 2027), order book Rs292cr -> tam=yes on carve-out. Winding-wire/conductor remains a commodity, LME metal pass-through, no pricing power -> moat=no (unchanged). P/E re-rated 26x->36.1x since last pass (screener/Sept 2026), mkt cap ~Rs607-658cr -> valuation=no, growth increasingly priced in. Score 2.0: 'un-ignorable growth' written exception keeps 10x-in-2-3-years, conviction capped Low-Medium/unconfirmed as already set.
